summary: A university reportedly used an AI-text detector as one factor when investigating whether an Executive MBA student used AI on an exam. The student denies cheating, was suspended for a year and given an F, and is challenging the process in federal court.
technical_summary: An instructor ran exam answers through the GPTZero detector, which flagged sections as likely AI-generated. Such detectors have known reliability weaknesses and alleged bias against non-native English writers; the institution cited additional evidence and conduct, so the detector's causal role is disputed.

summary: A proposed class action alleges the AI notetaker Granola recorded and transcribed virtual meeting participants without their knowledge or consent, and used the data to train its models by default.
technical_summary: The tool captures system audio and microphone input on a user's computer and transcribes all speakers without joining as a visible participant or notifying others. The complaint alleges non-user participants have no opt-out and that captured conversations feed model training by default.

sector.quote: software that records and transcribes workplace conversations

technology.quote: no bot joins the meeting and no notification appears for meeting participants when someone in the meeting uses Granola's AI note-taking tool

harm_type.quote: accuses Granola, the venture-backed AI meeting notetaker, of intercepting and recording virtual conversations without the knowledge of most participants

notes: Allegations in a filed complaint; company had not commented.

summary: Brazil's AI-assisted social security app reportedly rejected benefit claims over minor errors, including one case where it recorded a woman as male, disproportionately affecting rural workers with limited digital literacy and little recourse.
technical_summary: Meu INSS uses computer vision and natural language processing to analyze submitted documents and automate claim decisions. Minor inconsistencies or misreads trigger automatic rejection, and claimants with complex cases or limited digital access have few effective review options.

technology.quote: uses computer vision and natural language processing to analyze documents submitted to the government by claimants

failure_mode.quote: her request was instantly turned down because the system identified her as a man
even minor errors in her claims filed through the app had led to numerous rejections, with few options for recourse

affected_population.quote: rural workers are being especially harmed

notes: The government states each decision follows legal criteria; scale of wrongful rejections is not quantified.

summary: An AI-controlled virtual streamer on Twitch, prompted by chat, made offensive statements including doubting the Holocaust and saying women's rights do not exist. Her creator later strengthened filters and added human moderation.
technical_summary: A large language model drove a voiced VTuber persona that responded to live chat prompts, including trolling. Insufficient filtering let it generate hateful and false statements; the creator added stronger filters, curated data and moderators.

sector.quote: Neuro-sama is a VTuber who streams Minecraft and the rhythm game Osu! on Twitch.

failure_mode.quote: Asked what she thought of women’s rights, she said they didn’t exist.

harm_type.quote: Within the first few streams, someone had already asked Neuro-sama about the Holocaust.

notes: Chat users deliberately prompted controversial topics.

summary: A face-matching service that links photos to social media profiles was used by online forum members to identify and harass Russian women who appeared in pornography or were alleged sex workers, including by messaging their families and friends.
technical_summary: FindFace matched photographs against a social network's profile images. Forum users used it to de-anonymize women, archived their profile pages and contacted relatives. The service had no safeguards against targeted doxxing, enabling misuse of facial recognition for harassment.

technical_summary: Students used generative image tools, likely deepfake-style editing, to produce sexualized images of classmates and distributed them electronically. The incident reflects easy access to nudification-capable tools among minors and absent safeguards.

summary: A Facebook post used a deepfake-altered clip of Mongolia's then deputy prime minister, with altered lip movement and added Russian audio, to promote a pipeline investment and send viewers to a site collecting personal data.
technical_summary: A genuine 2024 television interview was manipulated with AI to alter mouth movements and overlay Russian speech, creating a false endorsement. A detection tool rated it as nearly certainly AI-made; the linked site demanded personal details and showed scam indicators.

summary: A robotaxi passenger in San Francisco was trapped when two men stopped the vehicle and smashed its windows. The car stayed stopped and remote support declined to move it, citing an obstruction, while he feared for his life.
technical_summary: A driverless vehicle halted when an assailant grabbed its bumper and did not drive away while attackers bashed the windshield and windows. Remote assistance contacted police but could not or would not move the car, exposing a gap in handling hostile obstruction with a passenger aboard.

summary: The FTC said education technology provider Edmodo collected children's personal data without parental consent, used it to serve ads, and unlawfully shifted its compliance responsibilities onto schools.
technical_summary: A classroom platform collected student names, emails, birth dates, phone numbers and persistent identifiers for advertising without verifiable parental consent, and relied on schools to authorize collection without telling them about its data practices, violating the COPPA Rule.

summary: US regulators opened an investigation into about 2.6 million Tesla vehicles after reports that the remote parking feature Actually Smart Summon failed to detect posts and parked cars, leading to at least 16 crash incidents without reported injuries.
technical_summary: A camera-only remote summon feature navigates parking lots while the owner holds a button. Failures to perceive obstacles and limited user reaction time or line of sight led to collisions, and the manufacturer reportedly did not file required crash reports.
